# PA-2.4 extraction notes (A2)

Text: pdftotext -layout of the supplied PDF, saved in _text/fulltext.txt; Table 5 (rotated page) re-extracted without layout in _text/p10_raw.txt. Page numbers are the journal pagination (141-151). The boldface marking of significant differences in Tables 2, 3 and 6 is lost in the text extraction, so significance per row cannot be checked from the text files; check the PDF.

## Rows proposed
- findings: 27 (N 22, Q 5). transformations: 1. claims: 25. relations: 5. decisions: header only.
- Joint claims proposed (Q and N roots): C10 only.

## Look at first
1. C10 (broader range of tools, p.150). Kept as one claim because the sentence asserts one thing (a broader range of tools) and lists examples ("including"). rests_on F7 and F25 (N: funding outside contracts; government leadership in noncontractual partnerships) and F10, F12, F13, F14 (Q: relationships, handshake norms, reputation). The body version (p.148-149, bulleted list of tools) uses the same material. If A1 applies rule 1 and splits per tool, each part becomes single-strand (funding N; norms, reputation, trust Q; shared goals no finding) and the study has no joint claim. fit proposed as expand: the interviews add tools that the survey does not measure.
2. C9 (little evidence that loss of formality equals loss of control, p.150). The conclusion gives no finding at that sentence; the body states equivalent conclusions from F7 (p.146 "partnerships without formal agreements but dependent on government funding are not necessarily outside the control of public managers") and F25 (p.149 "public managers are more likely to take the lead in partnerships without formal agreements"). The interviews (F14, p.147) also bear on control without contracts but are not linked to this conclusion by the text. Alternatives: rests_on empty with R2 only (C9 then rests on C10 via backs), or add F14 (C9 becomes joint).
3. C1 "led by government agencies" (abstract). Mapped to decision-making authority (F22, F25), not to the "lead organization" variable (F23, F24), which records the presence of a coordinator but not whether it is governmental (the author notes the difference, p.147). Government decision making is 52.1% overall (Table 5), so "most" holds only narrowly.
4. C2 "only weakly collaborative" (abstract) versus the body, p.146: "the activities that do occur vary widely and appear to be frequently collaborative in nature, in the sense of shared resources and decision-making effort." The body sentence is not a headline claim, so no relation is proposed; A1 may want to note the tension. The abstract claim is supported in the conclusion by shared decision making (C14), not by resource sharing; F4 and F9 were added for "resources".
5. C4 says "reported by public and nonprofit executives", but the "only half" figure (51.0%) is from the government survey only (Table 5, F21). The nonprofit figure (39.7% with a service contract, F5) is not about the most active partnership and is not cited; it is left out of rests_on (rule 3).
6. C5 split from C4 (rule 1): the value statement and the finding are separable; R1 records the link stated in the sentence. A1 may prefer one claim.
7. C25 (trust substitutes for formal agreements, p.151) cites recent scholarship; the study's own evidence for it is the interviews (F10, F12), which the text does not cite at this point. C3 (abstract, community norms substitute) rests on the same interviews. C3 and C25 are close in content; no relation proposed because the text does not link them.
8. C8 and C17 have empty rests_on. C8 ("glue" can be statutory, financial, relational) relates to F7 (financial), F10-F13 (relational) and F26 (state-supported agencies, p.149) but cites none of them. C17 follows C14 and C16 in the argument ("In short [...] Peters's notion [...] closer to the mark, and internal and external dimensions of control [...]"); a backs relation C14 to C16 or C17 was considered but not proposed, since the link is sequential rather than stated.
9. Research recommendations (C12, C18, C19, C20, C22, C23) are included as claims with empty rests_on, as for HLT-C2 C18. A1 may reject them as not headline claims. C21 (interviews preliminary) is a statement about the evidence; it backs C22 (R5).

## Excluded from claims
- Abstract statements of aims and method ("this study builds on B. Guy Peters's definition", "The agency theory notion [...] is also tested", "The study concludes with suggestions for further research regarding trust and behavioral norms"), p.141.
- Self-descriptions in the conclusion: "this article suggests ways to understand their defining features from a broader, multidimensional perspective", "this article addresses a key question for practitioners", "The study's methodological strength lies in its use of two large samples", "this study only nibbles at the edges of this larger theoretical debate", and the stated limitations (single state, nonprofit partners only, no matched responses), p.150-151.

## Transformations
- T on F27: Figure 1 (p.149) is built from Table 5 percentages (formality, shared versus government decision making) per policy area. Within strand N; crosses_strand no.
- No cross-strand transformation is reported: interview material is not counted or scored. The bulleted list of tools (p.149) combines survey and interview results narratively; it is recorded as the body version of C10, not as a transformation.

## Other
- Table 5 values were reconstructed from the rotated page; column order verified against the text (social 61.8% formal, 38.2% nonprofit-led; public safety 27.5% formal, 77.5% government; economic development 41.0% shared; environment 83.3% formal, 0% government; totals 51.0% formal, 52.1% government, 30.8% shared, 17.1% nonprofit, n=147).
- Table 6 results are described by the author as "preliminary" (p.148) owing to sample size.
- Quotes are verbatim from the extracted text with line-break hyphenation removed; "[...]" marks omissions. Quotes for F21 and F22 are table cells.

## Consistency pass (A3, 17 November 2026)
- Rule 11, C26 (merge of C2, C13, C15). Abstract p.141: "they are only weakly collaborative in the sense of shared authority or resources." Conclusion p.150: "This study finds less evidence of 'collaborative' partnerships. [...] In short, few of these partnerships can be described as partnerships between equals." Same assertion in three wordings. Rule 7/8: argued with findings in the conclusion through C14 ("lack a key ingredient of collaboration: shared decision making", F22, F25) and, for resources, p.146: "government agencies contribute financial and material resources [...] more frequently than do nonprofit organizations" (F9).
- F4 not carried into C26 (rule 3): F4 is about the scope of joint activity (number of activities), and the same paragraph (p.146) reads "the activities that do occur vary widely and appear to be frequently collaborative in nature, in the sense of shared resources and decision-making effort", which runs against the claim. The body sentence is not a headline claim, so no clash is recorded.
- Rule 10, R2 (C10 backs C9). p.150: "Little evidence is found here that loss of formality equals loss of control. This study finds that public managers have a broader range of tools [...]". No connective marks the link; sequence only.
- Rule 7 checked without change: C8 (no body passage argues that the 'glue' takes many forms; F7, F10-F13, F26 are thematic only, rule 8), C17 (no body passage on internal/external control versus institutional autonomy), C24 (literature only). C3 already rests on the interviews (p.147). C1 and C14 kept apart: government decision making (52.1%) and lack of shared decision making (69.2%) are different assertions. C3 and C25 kept apart: the text lists norms and trust as separate tools (p.149).
- Rules 9, 12, 13: not applicable (no instrument built from interviews or earlier results; no case-group comparison).
